title: Go SDK: streaming lifecycle adapter + context negotiation for cancellable timeouts
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: The current Go SDK has multiple ad-hoc places where context cancellation and per-message timeouts are handled by helpers sprinkled across the streaming layer. This causes: 1) inconsistent client-side behaviour for partial responses and shutdown; 2) unclear semantics for request-level vs. per-message deadlines; 3) fragile interactions with retries and reconnects.

Goal: Implement a centralized 'streaming lifecycle adapter' in the Go SDK that is responsible for: negotiating the effective deadline for a streaming session, propagating cancellations cleanly to underlying HTTP/websocket transports, exposing a clear API for callers to set request vs. per-message deadlines, and providing a deterministic graceful-teardown flow that preserves partial results when configured. The adapter should enable: - deterministic behaviour for context cancellation and timeouts - clear semantics for resumable vs non-resumable streams - easier testing and observability hooks (metrics/traces)

Non-goals: This ticket does not redesign the wire protocol or change server-side deadlines. We will not add new server-side resume tokens in this change.

Design notes: Proposed components: 1) LifecycleAdapter: top-level object created per stream call. Accepts parent context, userDeadline (optional), perMessageTimeout (optional), and flags: allowPartialOnCancel (bool), resumable (bool). 2) DeadlineNegotiator: merges parent context deadline, explicit userDeadline, and client-configured maxTTL to determine an effective stream deadline. 3) CancellationCoordinator: a small state machine that tracks states OPEN -> DRAINING -> CLOSED and sequences shutdown actions (stop read, flush buffers, signal accounter/metrics). 4) TransportAdapter: thin wrapper around http2/websocket client that listens to LifecycleAdapter cancellation and runs expedited close with reason codes.

API example (draft):
  ctx := context.Background()
  cfg := sdk.StreamConfig{PerMessageTimeout: 200*time.Millisecond, AllowPartialOnCancel: true, Resumable: true}
  stream, err := client.NewStreamingCall(ctx, req, cfg)
  // stream.Recv() will return partial responses when context is cancelled and AllowPartialOnCancel=true

Backward compatibility: keep existing NewStreamingCall(ctx, req) overloads with default config. The new adapter will be internal by default; public API additions are additive with sensible defaults.

Observability: lifecycleAdapter must emit metrics: stream_effective_deadline_seconds, stream_state_transitions, stream_cancel_reason, stream_partial_bytes_emitted. Add tracing spans for deadline_negotiation and shutdown_sequence.

Acceptance criteria: - unit tests cover negotiation logic across 6 deadline combinations - integration test simulating mid-stream context cancel returns partial data when allowed - benchmark shows <3% latency regression on happy-path 1K concurrent streams - clear doc comments and example snippet in README and godoc
comments: 2026-02-19 Maya Patel: Spiked an initial prototype to centralize deadlines in a single Negotiator. Observed a race when parent context had earlier deadline than per-message timeout — needs careful ordering.
2026-02-22 Liam O'Connor: Reviewed prototype; suggested we model Negotiator as immutable once created to simplify reasoning and avoid time-of-check/time-of-use races.

2026-02-25 Priya Singh (PM): Need to preserve old behaviour by default for a month after rollout; add feature flag 'streaming.lifecycle_adapter_v1' behind runtime flagging so we can flip if issues arise.

2026-03-02 Engineering review: Added CancellationCoordinator state machine (OPEN -> DRAINING -> CLOSED). Edge case: if transport-level close fails, coordinator must force-close after a bounded retry backoff and report telemetry.
2026-03-06 QA: Found flaky test where per-message timeouts overlapped with reconnect backoff. Plan: add deterministic clock in tests and stub out network delays.

2026-03-09 Security: Reviewed API surface. No secrets are retained by lifecycle adapter; KMS/HSM unaffected. Security reviewer asked for stronger docstring around context propagation to avoid misuse (do not use background context for request-scoped streams).

2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor: Implemented Negotiator immutability, added metrics hooks, and wrote first integration test. Pushing PR for internal review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/4123
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for DeadlineNegotiator covering parent-context-deadline, explicit-user-deadline, and max-ttl interactions
Integration test where mid-stream ctx cancel returns partial response when AllowPartialOnCancel=true
Benchmarks for 1k concurrent streams show <3% P95 latency regression
PR includes godoc examples and README section describing new config flags and backwards compatibility
Feature flag 'streaming.lifecycle_adapter_v1' is in place and default-off for one week canary rollout
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR behind feature flag. 2) Canary release to internal staging for 48h with telemetry dashboards. 3) Enable for 5% of production requests (routing rule) for 72h, monitor stream_error_rate and stream_partial_bytes_emitted. 4) Gradually increase to 50% then 100% if stable. 5) If issues, flip flag off and roll back patch.
qa_steps: Run unit test suite: go test ./... -run TestDeadlineNegotiator -race
Run integration harness with deterministic clock and simulate mid-stream cancel; verify partial data emitted when enabled
Run local benchmark harness: ./bench/stream_bench -concurrency=1000 and compare baseline metrics
Smoke test SDK examples in README with both AllowPartialOnCancel true/false
notes: Keep API additive. Avoid exposing internal state machine to public callers; use metrics and tracing to observe transitions.
Resumable=false mode should short-circuit Negotiator to prefer earliest deadline to avoid unnecessary retries.
Consider follow-up ticket to add server-side resume tokens if resumability becomes a priority for customers.
We should coordinate with SDK teams (Python/TS) to align behavior; add cross-SDK spec doc after stabilization.
